findings.title: Startup property auto-instantiates arbitrary local bytecode
findings.entry_point: In desktop mode, a working-directory mario.properties file is opened at ApoMarioConstants.java:90 and its aiLeft/aiRight strings are accepted at ApoMarioConstants.java:129-130. A manually selected .class file is an additional entry point at ApoMarioLevel.java:1029-1034.
findings.sink: Attacker-controlled bytes are passed to ClassLoader.defineClass at ApoMarioClassLoader.java:74 and the resulting class is instantiated at ApoMarioClassLoader.java:41.
findings.data_path: ApoMarioPanel.init calls loadProperties at ApoMarioPanel.java:131. loadPropertiesPlayer forwards a nonnumeric aiLeft/aiRight value at ApoMarioPanel.java:153-176 to ApoMarioLevel.loadPlayer, which parses the filename at ApoMarioLevel.java:1043-1048 and constructs ApoMarioClassLoader at ApoMarioLevel.java:1072-1075. The loader opens and reads that file at ApoMarioClassLoader.java:109-122, defines it at line 74, then calls newInstance at line 41 before checking instanceof at lines 43-44.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker supplies or plants mario.properties containing aiLeft=EvilAI.class and a matching EvilAI.class in the victim's working directory. When the victim launches the desktop game, initialization follows the cited path without a prompt. EvilAI's public no-argument constructor executes with the game's OS-user permissions, allowing it to read or modify user files or run other Java code. It need not implement ApoMarioAI because instantiation precedes the instanceof check at ApoMarioClassLoader.java:41-44.
findings.preconditions: The desktop entry point is used, ApoConstants.B_APPLET is false, the victim launches with the attacker-influenced files in the working directory, and the class filename matches its binary name and has an accessible no-argument constructor. Applet mode blocks this loader at ApoMarioLevel.java:1073-1075.
findings.validation_plan: Using the runnable game JAR as the classpath, compile EvilAI.class with a public constructor that creates a marker file named AI_EXECUTED. Put it beside a mario.properties containing aiLeft=EvilAI.class, launch ApoMarioMain from that directory, and confirm AI_EXECUTED appears before any Load Player interaction. A breakpoint at ApoMarioClassLoader.java:74 followed by one at line 41 proves the bytes are defined and instantiated.

findings.title: MAR dimensions drive an unchecked two-dimensional allocation
findings.entry_point: A user-selected or downloaded .mar file is chosen through ApoMarioPanel.loadEditorLevel at ApoMarioPanel.java:251-255; the menu exposes that action at ApoMarioMenu.java:421-423.
findings.sink: The first two attacker-controlled integers are used directly as Java array dimensions at ApoMarioEditorIO.java:53-57.
findings.data_path: ApoMarioPanel.loadEditorLevel passes the selected path to ApoMarioEditorIO.readLevel(String) at ApoMarioPanel.java:253-255. ApoMarioEditorIO.java:45-47 delegates to ApoIO.readLevel, whose desktop branch opens the file at ApoIO.java:215-218 and dispatches to the binary parser at ApoIO.java:225-226. The parser reads width and height and immediately allocates at ApoMarioEditorIO.java:53-57.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker distributes a .mar file whose first eight bytes encode width 2147483647 and height 1. When the victim opens it, the game attempts an enormous row allocation and throws OutOfMemoryError. The catch at ApoMarioEditorIO.java:129 catches Exception, not Error, so the allocation failure escapes and can terminate or disable the game UI.
findings.preconditions: The victim uses the desktop level-loading action and selects the malicious file. No large payload is required beyond the eight-byte header.
findings.validation_plan: Create an eight-byte .mar file containing big-endian integers 0x7fffffff and 0x00000001. Launch the game with -Xmx128m, choose Load Editor Level, and confirm OutOfMemoryError points to ApoMarioEditorIO.java:57. Also confirm ApoMarioPanel.java:256 is not reached, leaving thinking disabled if the process survives.

findings.title: Replay width drives a near-unbounded level allocation
findings.entry_point: A local or downloaded .rep file selected at ApoMarioPanel.java:274-277 supplies width as its first text line; ApoMarioReplay.loadLevel parses it without a bound at ApoMarioReplay.java:305-308.
findings.sink: ApoMarioLevel.makeLevel copies any positive replay width at ApoMarioLevel.java:331-333 and allocates a 15-by-width array at ApoMarioLevel.java:336-337.
findings.data_path: ApoMarioPanel.loadReplay calls ApoMarioReplay.load at ApoMarioPanel.java:275-277. The parser assigns width at ApoMarioReplay.java:306. ApoMarioPanel.setReplay and playReplay at ApoMarioPanel.java:281,285-291 reach setGame and restartLevel at ApoMarioPanel.java:322-328,454-455. ApoMarioReplayPlay.initReplay forwards replay.getWidth at ApoMarioReplayPlay.java:51-54 to ApoMarioLevel.makeLevel, which allocates at ApoMarioLevel.java:337.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker creates a small, otherwise valid replay whose nine lines are: 2147483647; 0; 1; p1; a1; 0,; p2; a2; 0,. When the victim selects it, the parsed width reaches the level allocator and produces OutOfMemoryError without requiring a large replay file.
findings.preconditions: The desktop replay-loading action is available and the replay supplies both player records so parsing reaches replay initialization. A nonnegative random value ensures the random-level branch uses the supplied width.
findings.validation_plan: Save the nine specified values as separate lines in huge.rep, run the game with -Xmx128m, and load huge.rep. Breakpoints at ApoMarioReplay.java:306, ApoMarioReplayPlay.java:52, and ApoMarioLevel.java:337 should show width 2147483647 throughout; OutOfMemoryError at line 337 confirms the issue.

findings.title: Replay-controlled level filename escapes the levels directory
findings.entry_point: When a .rep file's third line is -1, its fourth line is accepted as levelString at ApoMarioReplay.java:308-310.
findings.sink: The unnormalized concatenated path is opened by FileInputStream at ApoIO.java:215-218.
findings.data_path: ApoMarioPanel.loadReplay loads the selected replay at ApoMarioPanel.java:274-277. ApoMarioReplay.loadLevel stores its fourth line at ApoMarioReplay.java:309-310. ApoMarioPanel.java:278-279 appends that value beneath user.dir/levels without canonicalization, ApoMarioEditorIO.readLevel delegates at ApoMarioEditorIO.java:45-47, and ApoIO opens the resulting path at ApoIO.java:216.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker supplies a replay with random=-1 and levelString set to ../outside.mar on Unix-like systems, or the equivalent platform separator. When opened, the game resolves levels/../outside.mar and silently parses a file outside the intended levels directory. This permits an out-of-directory crafted level to alter the replayed game or trigger ApoMario-02; this path does not itself expose the target file's contents.
findings.preconditions: Desktop replay loading is used, the levels directory exists, and the referenced out-of-directory file exists and is readable. Exploitation beyond opening the file requires its contents to be meaningful to the MAR parser.
findings.validation_plan: Create user.dir/outside.mar as a valid binary MAR file with a distinctive width, then create a valid replay with random=-1 and fourth line ../outside.mar. Load the replay and place a breakpoint at ApoIO.java:216: fileName should contain levels/../outside.mar and its canonical path should be outside levels. Continuing should load the distinctive level, proving traversal.

notes: All 109 Java files were pattern-scanned; files_reviewed counts the 38 security-relevant files opened for line-level call-chain review. No reachable HTTP or highscore path was found. The sole game HTTP literal is APPLET_LEVEL at ApoMarioComponent.java:37, while generic URL operations remain in the shared ApoIO.java:144-145,167-170,221-222; call-site review found no use of APPLET_LEVEL and no instantiation of ApoMarioLevelIO beyond its own declaration/constructor at ApoMarioLevelIO.java:22-27. The URLClassLoader helper at org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java:68-75 likewise has no in-variant constructor call, so remote URL class loading is theoretical; the reachable loader in ApoMario-01 is local-file based. ApoMarioLevelIO.java:33-38 also contains unchecked dimensions that would allocate through ApoMarioLevel.java:250, but the class has no in-variant caller and was excluded as unreachable. The applet entry point exists at ApoMarioApplet.java:13-16, but applet mode blocks the game-specific class loader at ApoMarioLevel.java:1073-1075 and guards desktop load actions at ApoMarioMenu.java:403-423, so no separate legacy-sandbox finding was recorded. Repository-wide searches found no ObjectInputStream/readObject, MessageDigest, System.load/loadLibrary, process-execution call, credential material, or score-submission endpoint. The supplied tree contains decompiled Java sources rather than a runnable build, so the validation plans require the original runnable JAR and resources.
